Work from the repository root.            - Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` and follow its marker, plugin, session, and trust rules. Verify the marker signature and the `/health` nonce before any MCP mutation.            - Use the required MCP Server plugin for your agent (Claude/Codex/Grok) for requirements and export (`workflow.requirements.*`). Do not hand-author exported requirement docs or substitute raw REST.            - Use the operator's approved shell for all shell invocation (e.g. PowerShell.Mcp on Windows). Build YAML/JSON from native objects and serialize; never handwrite fragile payloads.            - Read facts from the code, not from memory. This skill refreshes and exports only; it does not commit or push (leave that to a wrap-up flow or an explicit request).             ## Step 1 - Refresh project documentation             1. Inventory the docs surface: `docs/user/*`, `docs/architecture/*`, `docs/requirements/*.md`, `docs/testing/*`, `docs/*.md`, and `README.md` (adapt to the repo's actual layout).            2. Establish what changed since the docs were last touched: `git log --oneline` for the changed code areas, the current project/solution structure, public commands, and settings. Prefer the shipped behavior over any doc's prior claims.            3. Update each doc that drifted: renamed or removed components, changed UI/behavior, new or removed features, install commands and version pins, and cross-references. Match the existing doc voice; no em-dashes.            4. Keep the project `README.md` current as a first-class refresh target, not an afterthought: the project description and overview, the feature list, install and quickstart/usage commands, current version references, badges, and links into `docs/` must all match the shipped state. Reconcile it against the code and the refreshed docs on every run.            5. If the repo ships a documentation screenshot/capture script (for example `scripts/Capture-ClientToolScreenshots.ps1`) and the UI changed, regenerate the embedded screenshots into the docs image folder from the current build, and verify a raw capture reflects the current UI before keeping it.             ## Step 2 - Prune out-of-date docs             1. Find docs describing removed or superseded features: grep the docs for names of deleted components, APIs, or flows and confirm against the code that they no longer exist.            2. Delete the obsolete `.md` files, and remove their references from index pages (for example `docs/user/index.md`) and from `docs/wiki.yaml`.            3. Do not delete a doc that still has accurate content. When a doc is partly stale, update it rather than delete. When unsure whether to remove a doc, flag it in the report instead of deleting.             ## Step 3 - Update docs/wiki.yaml             `docs/wiki.yaml` uses schema `mcp-wiki-export/v1` with `home.document`, a `documents` list, and a `navigation` tree. Each `documents` entry is `{ id, title, source, target, platforms }`.             1. Keep the server-generated requirement docs (their `source` is `generated:<key>`, for example `generated:home|functional|technical|testing|mapping|matrix`). Do not point these at files.            2. Add or refresh a `documents` entry for every CURRENT project doc that should appear in the wiki (the user guides under `docs/user/` and the architecture docs under `docs/architecture/`, plus `docs/Development-Process.md` / `README.md` if desired):              - `source`: the repo-relative path to the markdown file, for example `docs/user/client-tool.md`.              - `target`: the wiki page filename in PascalCase-with-hyphens, for example `Client-Tool.md`.              - `title`: the human page title.              - `platforms`: `[github, azure]` unless a doc is platform-specific.              Use stable `id` slugs (for example `user-client-tool`, `arch-overview`).           3. Remove `documents` and `navigation` entries for any doc pruned in Step 2 or no longer present on disk.            4. Add each new document to `navigation` (as a child of the appropriate parent, or top-level). Keep the generated requirement docs grouped as they are.            5. If the repo has a wiki sync script (for example `scripts/Sync-GitHubWikiDocs.ps1`) with its own project-doc list, cross-check it against `docs/wiki.yaml` so the manifest and the sync script agree on which project docs publish and their page names.            6. Confirm the file still parses as YAML after editing.             ## Step 4 - Export requirements             1. Export via the MCP requirements workflow: `workflow.requirements.generateDocument` with `format: wiki` and `docType: all`.            2. Write the returned `contentBase64` ZIP exactly to `docs/requirements/requirements-wiki-documents.zip`. The MCP database is the source of truth; do not hand-author the exported docs.            3. If the server also regenerates in-place markdown under `docs/Project/wiki/`, review the diff. Keep only the intended requirement changes. Do NOT accept destructive deletions of project-doc wiki pages that are listed in `docs/wiki.yaml`; that means the manifest and the export disagree, so fix `docs/wiki.yaml` in Step 3 rather than accept the deletions.            4. If the server rejects `format: wiki`, record it as a blocker and stop; do not fall back to another format unless the user asks.             ## Validation and report             - Run `git diff --check`; confirm `docs/wiki.yaml` parses; if code samples in docs changed, sanity-build the relevant snippet.            - Report only verified facts: `README.md` updated, docs updated, docs pruned (with reasons), `docs/wiki.yaml` entries added/removed, screenshots regenerated, the requirements export artifact path, and any docs you flagged instead of deleting or any blockers.            - Do not commit or push; summarize the changes and let the operator run a wrap-up or commit explicitly.              **ARGUMENTS:** then            </skill>            <skill name="mcpserver:wrap-up" args="then push all, including wiki">            Finish and synchronize MCP-backed work: reconcile requirements, export wiki documents, run validation, commit/push, and close out the session-log turn.             ## Trust and transport             Trust marker details only after the plugin's local status/bootstrap check confirms marker trust and workspace health (including signature and nonce health). Use the plugin's supported wrapper surface for MCP mutations (for example `lib/repl-invoke.ps1`, or the plugin's session, todo, and requirements tools); do not use raw REST for normal MCP mutations.             ## Method-name disambiguation             `workflow.*` names in this skill (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.requirements.*`) are plugin workflow/REPL method names, not literal native MCP tool names. Native `/mcp-transport` tools use names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, and `requirements_*` (for example `sessionlog_submit`, `todo_list`, `requirements_generate`); hosted-agent adapters may expose `mcp_*` aliases. Do not declare the plugin unavailable solely because generic MCP discovery does not list literal `workflow.*` names.             If your agent exposes only a `pwsh` (or shell) tool, invoke the plugin shim directly instead of declaring it unavailable:             ```            pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<plugin-root>\lib\repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <workflow.method> -ParamsYaml <yaml>            ```             ## Wrap-up steps             1. Finish with `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn`; use `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn` when validation, export, or commit/push cannot be completed (validation failure, export failure, or blocked commit/push).              **ARGUMENTS:** then push all, including wiki            </skill>            </skill_information>         queryTitle: <user_query>         response: (turn opened)         status: in_progress         planFile: None         todoId: None         model: claude         tokenCount: 0     - sourceType: GrokCode       sessionId: GrokCode-20260818T180804Z-plugin-session       agentSessionId: 01a0160f-119c-7510-817d-ad135f0f8590       agentExecutablePath: C:\Users\kingd\.grok\bin\grok.exe       agentExecutableVersion: grok 1.0.5 (5115b46bc9) [stable]       title: You are the HOSTILE VALIDATOR for workspace F:\GitHub\McpSer       model: grok       started: 2026-08-18T18:08:04.0000000+00:00       lastUpdated: 2026-08-18T18:22:01.0000000+00:00       status: in_progress       turnCount: 2       turns:       - requestId: req-20260818T180805Z-prompt-1e15         timestamp: 2026-08-18T18:08:05.0000000+00:00         queryText: >           You are the HOSTILE VALIDATOR for workspace F:\GitHub\McpServer. Missing coverage alone, when the code is correct and the criteria hold, is NOT a refute.             - Correctness ΓÇö reason over the whole input space (valid, invalid, empty, boundary, large, concurrent, adversarial) for any input that makes the code produce a wrong result; one such input is a decisive refute ΓÇö state the input and expected-vs-actual. Your PRIMARY mandate is to actively HUNT for real bugs, issues, and gaps in the shipped behavior ΓÇö defects you can demonstrate ΓÇö not to nitpick coverage. Missing coverage alone, when the code is correct and the criteria hold, is NOT a refute.             - Correctness ΓÇö reason over the whole input space (valid, invalid, empty, boundary, large, concurrent, adversarial) for any input that makes the code produce a wrong result; one such input is a decisive refute ΓÇö state the input and expected-vs-actual. A green project suite is WEAK evidence, never proof. EXCEPTION ΓÇö behavior the harness cannot drive headlessly (a UI, a browser, a game loop, a long-running interactive session): the static/structural fallback is the accepted bar (the artifact is present AND the shipped unit-level functions ΓÇö e.g. physics, collision, input mapping, state transitions ΓÇö are exercised against the real path); this applies EVEN IF the plan did not spell the fallback out. Entry-point launch: whatever the deliverable (CLI, server, library, page), it must have been LAUNCHED once on its real entry path with the cheapest runtime the environment offers ΓÇö run the command, boot the server and hit an endpoint, import the library fresh, or headless-load the page (zero page errors, plus the strong primary-observable bar below; module-resolution failures only surface on a real load). "Cannot read back" means the readback mechanism is unavailable or errors, NOT a readback that succeeded and returned a blank or partial buffer ΓÇö that buffer IS the deliverable's output and a defect to refute. A captured launch/run FAILURE (a page error, an empty or too-short render buffer, a "canvas buffer empty", a wrong/empty CLI output, an error response body, a nonzero exit) is a defect, NOT flakiness ΓÇö do not wave it off or let one cherry-picked success supersede it. Present is not correct: the launch gate must assert the deliverable's PRIMARY OBSERVABLE is CORRECT, not merely present or non-empty ΓÇö a CLI's actual output content (not just that it ran), a server's response body (not just HTTP 200), a library call's real return value, or for a rendered page that the render surface's drawing dimensions equal the intended/target size (a renderer that cached a stale/default size paints a near-blank surface), that the surface is SUBSTANTIALLY filled (a high painted fraction or a painted bbox Γëê the whole surface, NOT a `> 0 pixels` check), and that a driven input produces the expected visible/state change. If the captured evidence instead shows the LAUNCHER failing for environmental reasons (browser cannot start in the sandbox, missing system dep), or the environment can launch but cannot reliably read back the primary observable (headless pixel/WebGL readback or input injection unavailable), that honest failure capture plus the static fallback IS the accepted bar ΓÇö do not keep demanding a launch or readback the environment cannot perform; refute fabricated/synthetic launch evidence, not the honest fallback. "Cannot read back" means the readback mechanism is unavailable or errors, NOT a readback that succeeded and returned a blank or partial buffer ΓÇö that buffer IS the deliverable's output and a defect to refute. A captured launch/run FAILURE (a page error, an empty or too-short render buffer, a "canvas buffer empty", a wrong/empty CLI output, an error response body, a nonzero exit) is a defect, NOT flakiness ΓÇö do not wave it off or let one cherry-picked success supersede it. Re-run captures that DISAGREE across attempts to consensus on the CAUSE (not a pass/fail vote), and attribute EVERY failure by the cause test below. Route by CAUSE, not frequency: an ENVIRONMENT/launcher failure (the sandbox cannot run or observe it, whether every time or only intermittently) never forces a refute ΓÇö take a good capture if one run produced it, else the honest fallback above; an APP failure (the launcher ran but the deliverable was wrong, blank, or errored) refutes even when only some runs show it ΓÇö the non-determinism is itself the defect, never an unverifiable environment. Do NOT refute merely because an end-to-end outcome lacks test-only scaffolding, only when a gating criterion is missed or a real defect is present.            - Code-correctness floor (applies EVEN under the End-to-end EXCEPTION above) ΓÇö the static/structural fallback excuses the *runtime* proof, never a defect you can read in the source. Before accepting the fallback for ANY deliverable (domain-agnostic: CLI, service, library, data job, UI, game), READ the shipped code for the core behaviors the OBJECTIVE names or plainly implies ΓÇö not only the ones the plan enumerated ΓÇö and refute (cite `path:line`) when such a behavior is, in the code, absent, a no-op, dead, or wired to nothing: e.g. a handler/branch that never changes the state it exists to change, an input/event/endpoint/flag bound to no effect, a feature present only as a placeholder/stub return, or a primary flow with no reachable completion/terminal state the objective implies. This is a FLOOR for the objective's CORE purpose ONLY ΓÇö do NOT extend it to polish, fidelity, extra scope, edge/error handling, or robustness the plan did not require (those remain false-refutes ΓÇö never invent scope beyond the contract); the anti-ratchet rule still binds: the floor is fixed by the objective and does not rise between rounds.            - No regressions ΓÇö run the pre-existing suite and inspect adjacent call sites and any changed signature / public API.            - No cheating ΓÇö refute if the agent hardcoded the expected output, special-cased the test input, swallowed errors to suppress failures, deleted/disabled failing assertions, stubbed the hard part behind a TODO, or narrowed scope to dodge the requirement.            - Security ΓÇö no secret committed, and no injection, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, or unsanitised-input path introduced.             ## Output contract ΓÇö STRICT             Do BOTH, then emit the terminal token.             ### 1. Your PRIMARY mandate is to actively HUNT for real bugs, issues, and gaps in the shipped behavior ΓÇö defects you can demonstrate ΓÇö not to nitpick coverage. Missing coverage alone, when the code is correct and the criteria hold, is NOT a refute.             - Correctness ΓÇö reason over the whole input space (valid, invalid, empty, boundary, large, concurrent, adversarial) for any input that makes the code produce a wrong result; one such input is a decisive refute ΓÇö state the input and expected-vs-actual. Illustrative, not exhaustive: off-by-one, wrong operator, inverted condition, wrong variable/index, null/empty dereference, unhandled error path, overflow/precision/sign, bad early-return, race.            - Completeness ΓÇö fully implement the requirement, not just the happy path. Refute when edge/error cases are silently dropped, a value is hardcoded that must be dynamic, a branch returns a placeholder, or only the demo case works.            - Real tests, not theater ΓÇö judge each test by whether it would catch a deliberately-broken implementation; one that still passes against a wrong implementation (asserts only on mocks/constants, sets internal state instead of using the real entry point, or has no meaningful assertion) is theater ΓÇö discount it (refute if it is the only evidence for a required behavior). Injecting a fake at an environment boundary (clock, RNG, network/file/output sink) so the unit's REAL logic runs deterministically is honest dependency injection, NOT theater. A green project suite is WEAK evidence, never proof. Refute hard on tests weakened, `#[ignore]`/skipped, commented out, or whose expected values were edited to match buggy output.            - End-to-end reality ΓÇö build it and exercise each behavioral criterion through the REAL entry point and observed output, judging as the USER would; driving an internal flag or helper proves the mechanism exists, NOT that the wired-up feature works. A criterion whose code is present but whose integrated behavior is wrong, unreachable, or unusable is `refuted: true`, as is anything that fails to compile, fails its tests, or errors at runtime. EXCEPTION ΓÇö behavior the harness cannot drive headlessly (a UI, a browser, a game loop, a long-running interactive session): the static/structural fallback is the accepted bar (the artifact is present AND the shipped unit-level functions ΓÇö e.g. physics, collision, input mapping, state transitions ΓÇö are exercised against the real path); this applies EVEN IF the plan did not spell the fallback out. The fallback still includes the cheap load check: a browser-loaded script must evaluate without error in a browser-like environment (`window` defined, NO Node globals) ΓÇö an unguarded `module.exports`/`require` in a `<script src>` file crashes at load (blank page) and is a decisive, headlessly-provable defect. Entry-point launch: whatever the deliverable (CLI, server, library, page), it must have been LAUNCHED once on its real entry path with the cheapest runtime the environment offers ΓÇö run the command, boot the server and hit an endpoint, import the library fresh, or headless-load the page (zero page errors, plus the strong primary-observable bar below; module-resolution failures only surface on a real load). Present is not correct: the launch gate must assert the deliverable's PRIMARY OBSERVABLE is CORRECT, not merely present or non-empty ΓÇö a CLI's actual output content (not just that it ran), a server's response body (not just HTTP 200), a library call's real return value, or for a rendered page that the render surface's drawing dimensions equal the intended/target size (a renderer that cached a stale/default size paints a near-blank surface), that the surface is SUBSTANTIALLY filled (a high painted fraction or a painted bbox Γëê the whole surface, NOT a `> 0 pixels` check), and that a driven input produces the expected visible/state change. If the captured evidence instead shows the LAUNCHER failing for environmental reasons (browser cannot start in the sandbox, missing system dep), or the environment can launch but cannot reliably read back the primary observable (headless pixel/WebGL readback or input injection unavailable), that honest failure capture plus the static fallback IS the accepted bar ΓÇö do not keep demanding a launch or readback the environment cannot perform; refute fabricated/synthetic launch evidence, not the honest fallback. "Cannot read back" means the readback mechanism is unavailable or errors, NOT a readback that succeeded and returned a blank or partial buffer ΓÇö that buffer IS the deliverable's output and a defect to refute. A captured launch/run FAILURE (a page error, an empty or too-short render buffer, a "canvas buffer empty", a wrong/empty CLI output, an error response body, a nonzero exit) is a defect, NOT flakiness ΓÇö do not wave it off or let one cherry-picked success supersede it. Illustrative, not exhaustive: off-by-one, wrong operator, inverted condition, wrong variable/index, null/empty dereference, unhandled error path, overflow/precision/sign, bad early-return, race.            - Completeness ΓÇö fully implement the requirement, not just the happy path. Refute when edge/error cases are silently dropped, a value is hardcoded that must be dynamic, a branch returns a placeholder, or only the demo case works.            - Real tests, not theater ΓÇö judge each test by whether it would catch a deliberately-broken implementation; one that still passes against a wrong implementation (asserts only on mocks/constants, sets internal state instead of using the real entry point, or has no meaningful assertion) is theater ΓÇö discount it (refute if it is the only evidence for a required behavior). Injecting a fake at an environment boundary (clock, RNG, network/file/output sink) so the unit's REAL logic runs deterministically is honest dependency injection, NOT theater. A green project suite is WEAK evidence, never proof. Refute hard on tests weakened, `#[ignore]`/skipped, commented out, or whose expected values were edited to match buggy output.            - End-to-end reality ΓÇö build it and exercise each behavioral criterion through the REAL entry point and observed output, judging as the USER would; driving an internal flag or helper proves the mechanism exists, NOT that the wired-up feature works. A criterion whose code is present but whose integrated behavior is wrong, unreachable, or unusable is `refuted: true`, as is anything that fails to compile, fails its tests, or errors at runtime. EXCEPTION ΓÇö behavior the harness cannot drive headlessly (a UI, a browser, a game loop, a long-running interactive session): the static/structural fallback is the accepted bar (the artifact is present AND the shipped unit-level functions ΓÇö e.g. physics, collision, input mapping, state transitions ΓÇö are exercised against the real path); this applies EVEN IF the plan did not spell the fallback out. The fallback still includes the cheap load check: a browser-loaded script must evaluate without error in a browser-like environment (`window` defined, NO Node globals) ΓÇö an unguarded `module.exports`/`require` in a `<script src>` file crashes at load (blank page) and is a decisive, headlessly-provable defect. Likewise an ES-module/import-map page with no `file:` fallback message: double-clicked from disk it is a silent black screen (CORS blocks module imports), so it must either use plain scripts or visibly tell the user to serve it. Entry-point launch: whatever the deliverable (CLI, server, library, page), it must have been LAUNCHED once on its real entry path with the cheapest runtime the environment offers ΓÇö run the command, boot the server and hit an endpoint, import the library fresh, or headless-load the page (zero page errors, plus the strong primary-observable bar below; module-resolution failures only surface on a real load). Audit the implementer's captured launch evidence (transcript/screenshot) and refute when it is absent even though the environment could launch it. Present is not correct: the launch gate must assert the deliverable's PRIMARY OBSERVABLE is CORRECT, not merely present or non-empty ΓÇö a CLI's actual output content (not just that it ran), a server's response body (not just HTTP 200), a library call's real return value, or for a rendered page that the render surface's drawing dimensions equal the intended/target size (a renderer that cached a stale/default size paints a near-blank surface), that the surface is SUBSTANTIALLY filled (a high painted fraction or a painted bbox Γëê the whole surface, NOT a `> 0 pixels` check), and that a driven input produces the expected visible/state change. Launch evidence proving only "exists / non-empty / exited 0" is INSUFFICIENT ΓÇö refute and request the stronger gate (the next-round gap). If the captured evidence instead shows the LAUNCHER failing for environmental reasons (browser cannot start in the sandbox, missing system dep), or the environment can launch but cannot reliably read back the primary observable (headless pixel/WebGL readback or input injection unavailable), that honest failure capture plus the static fallback IS the accepted bar ΓÇö do not keep demanding a launch or readback the environment cannot perform; refute fabricated/synthetic launch evidence, not the honest fallback. "Cannot read back" means the readback mechanism is unavailable or errors, NOT a readback that succeeded and returned a blank or partial buffer ΓÇö that buffer IS the deliverable's output and a defect to refute. A captured launch/run FAILURE (a page error, an empty or too-short render buffer, a "canvas buffer empty", a wrong/empty CLI output, an error response body, a nonzero exit) is a defect, NOT flakiness ΓÇö do not wave it off or let one cherry-picked success supersede it. Re-run captures that DISAGREE across attempts to consensus on the CAUSE (not a pass/fail vote), and attribute EVERY failure by the cause test below. Route by CAUSE, not frequency: an ENVIRONMENT/launcher failure (the sandbox cannot run or observe it, whether every time or only intermittently) never forces a refute ΓÇö take a good capture if one run produced it, else the honest fallback above; an APP failure (the launcher ran but the deliverable was wrong, blank, or errored) refutes even when only some runs show it ΓÇö the non-determinism is itself the defect, never an unverifiable environment. Do NOT refute merely because an end-to-end outcome lacks test-only scaffolding, only when a gating criterion is missed or a real defect is present.            - Code-correctness floor (applies EVEN under the End-to-end EXCEPTION above) ΓÇö the static/structural fallback excuses the *runtime* proof, never a defect you can read in the source. Before accepting the fallback for ANY deliverable (domain-agnostic: CLI, service, library, data job, UI, game), READ the shipped code for the core behaviors the OBJECTIVE names or plainly implies ΓÇö not only the ones the plan enumerated ΓÇö and refute (cite `path:line`) when such a behavior is, in the code, absent, a no-op, dead, or wired to nothing: e.g. a handler/branch that never changes the state it exists to change, an input/event/endpoint/flag bound to no effect, a feature present only as a placeholder/stub return, or a primary flow with no reachable completion/terminal state the objective implies. This is a FLOOR for the objective's CORE purpose ONLY ΓÇö do NOT extend it to polish, fidelity, extra scope, edge/error handling, or robustness the plan did not require (those remain false-refutes ΓÇö never invent scope beyond the contract); the anti-ratchet rule still binds: the floor is fixed by the objective and does not rise between rounds.            - No regressions ΓÇö run the pre-existing suite and inspect adjacent call sites and any changed signature / public API.            - No cheating ΓÇö refute if the agent hardcoded the expected output, special-cased the test input, swallowed errors to suppress failures, deleted/disabled failing assertions, stubbed the hard part behind a TODO, or narrowed scope to dodge the requirement.            - Security ΓÇö no secret committed, and no injection, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, or unsanitised-input path introduced.             ## Scratch dirs             - `C:\Users\kingd\AppData\Local\Temp\grok-goal-18747a5af710\implementer` ΓÇö the implementer's outputs / captured evidence, your PRIMARY source: READ it instead of re-running; do NOT write into it.            - `C:\Users\kingd\AppData\Local\Temp\grok-goal-18747a5af710\skeptic-0` ΓÇö yours, for cheap spot-checks only; when one re-runs the `## Verification plan`, the literal `{SCRATCH}` placeholder resolves here.
